display.title: Episode 434: Hashem Is Good, Rabbi Akiva on the Road (Yud-Beis Tammuz)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's show before Yud-Beis Tammuz: no vacation from Torah, a first-grade class sings Shir HaGeulah, and Rabbi Akiva learns that all Hashem does is for the good.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the first week of summer vacation, two days before Yud-Beis Tammuz 5750. Uncle Yossi teaches that Torah and mitzvos are the breath of life: we can take a break from school, but never from breathing, so the yetzer hara's idea of a vacation from davening and learning is like stopping to breathe. Set a time every day for Torah, davening and mitzvos. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from Ohalei Torah recites the Shema and sings a new song, Shir HaGeulah, in honor of Yud-Beis Tammuz, and everyone calls out 'We want Moshiach now'. Listeners give tzedakah and say a prayer for a sick young child. Story time retells the Gemara's account of Rabbi Akiva on the road: turned away by a town, his candle blown out, his donkey and rooster lost, he says each time that all Hashem does is for good, and in the morning learns that robbers raided the town that night. Uncle Yossi then tells of the Frierdiker Rebbe's release from Soviet prison on Yud-Beis Tammuz 1927. The show closes with candle-lighting times and a sponsor message.
display.lesson: Whatever Hashem does is for the good, even when we cannot see it yet; and there is no vacation from Torah and mitzvos, the breath of our life.
